# BirJS documentation

Source: https://birjs.com/docs/ai-rules

# AI Assistant Guide

Download the application guide and add it to your coding assistant's project context. Match examples to the version installed in your application.

- [Application guide](/BIRFRAMEWORK_RULES.md)
- [Cursor rules file](/.cursorrules)
- [Documentation index](/llms.txt)
- [Complete documentation](/llms-full.txt)

The downloadable guide and the text below are maintained together.

## Application guide

This guide describes the local framework API. Check the installed package version and its declarations before using an API from another release.

## Runtime and entry points

Use Node.js 22.5 or later. Create a project with `npx birframework new my-app --ts --tailwind --inertia`. Use --js for JavaScript or --server-rendered for server-rendered views. Generate APP_KEY with `npx bir key:generate`.

An Application can register middleware and routes. Keep bootstrap export separate from the entry that calls listen when importing it into tests. app.serverless() returns a serverless handler.

## HTTP

Import Context from birframework. Read input with `await ctx.body()` and validate with `await ctx.validate(rules)`. ctx.params contains path values and ctx.query contains query values. Respond with ctx.json(data, status), ctx.text(), ctx.html(), ctx.redirect(), ctx.inertia(), or ctx.render(). Set response headers with ctx.header(name, value).

```ts
import { Route } from 'birframework';

Route.post('/contact', async (ctx) => {
  const data = await ctx.validate({ email: 'required|email' });
  return ctx.json({ email: data.email }, 201);
});
```

## Middleware and sessions

The middleware signature is (ctx: Context, next: Next). Import Context and Next as types. Await next(). Register sessionMiddleware() before using ctx.session or csrf(). Pass csrfToken(ctx) to page props and include a hidden _token input in forms or X-CSRF-TOKEN in requests.

FileSessionStore takes a directory string. sessionMiddleware({ driver: 'file', storeDir: 'storage/framework/sessions' }) selects it directly. An in-memory store is process-local. Serverless /tmp storage is instance-local.

## Models and database

```ts
import { Model } from 'birframework';

export class User extends Model {
  static table = 'users';
  static fillable = ['name', 'email'];
}

const users = await User.query().orderBy('id', 'desc').get();
const page = await User.paginate({ page: 1, perPage: 15 });
console.log(page.data, page.meta.total);
```

The default connection reads DB_CONNECTION and DB_DATABASE. PostgreSQL and MySQL also read DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USERNAME, DB_PASSWORD, or DATABASE_URL. Install pg or mysql2 for those drivers. DB.raw(sql, bindings) queries SQL. DB.execute performs writes. DB.table(name) returns a query builder. DB.transaction(async () => ...) manages a transaction.

Migrations export up/down functions or a default object/class with up/down. Use Schema.create and Blueprint column helpers. Column defaults use .default(value).

## Authentication

Auth.attempt(ctx, credentials, User) requires the user model. Auth.user(ctx, User) resolves the current user. Use auth() middleware for access checks. Model fillable and guarded are static properties.

## Pages and components

Inertia pages live in views/pages and use ctx.inertia('Page', props). Server-rendered views use ctx.render('View', props). Both use Preact TSX/JSX. Reusable components live in views/components. Browser events require hydration. Access browser globals in handlers or effects.

Import Link, router, useForm, usePage, and Head from the generated resources/js/bir-inertia module using the correct relative path. Use persistent Page.layout only for UI that should remain mounted. Register birVite() in Vite plugins to discover the development asset port. Production assets use the build manifest.

## Jobs and scheduling

Dispatch with dispatch(new MyJob()) and delay with .delay(seconds). Register job classes through Queue.register(MyJob) in app/jobs/index.ts or .js so the worker can deserialize them. Start the worker with npx bir queue:work.

Import schedule definitions in the same process that calls Schedule.work(). The schedule CLI does not automatically discover application definitions. Use implemented interval helpers or dailyAt. Cross-process overlap locks require shared filesystem storage.

## Mail and storage

Mail.to(address).send() accepts a Mailable. For HTML strings use Mail.to(address).raw(html, { subject }). Mailable.view returns a promise, so content can be async. Escape user-controlled HTML text. Storage.disk(name) selects local, public, or configured cloud storage.

## Tests and documentation

Use node:test and createTestClient for HTTP tests. Close the client after tests. Import a bootstrap Application without opening a listener. Read the topic documentation for configuration and complete examples. Avoid invented APIs and performance guarantees.


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/auth

# Authentication & Sessions

BirJS provides built-in authentication services, secure cryptographically signed cookies, session handling, and a full-stack starter kit inspired by Laravel Breeze.

---

## Instant Auth Starter Kit (`make:auth`)

To scaffold a complete, production-ready authentication system with login, registration, password hashing, dashboard, and Tailwind CSS views in seconds:

```bash
npx birframework make:auth
```

This single command automatically scaffolds:
- `app/models/User.ts` (Active Record User model)
- `database/migrations/*_create_users_table.ts` (Schema migration)
- `app/controllers/AuthController.ts` (Login, Register, and Logout actions)
- `views/auth/login.tsx` & `views/auth/register.tsx` (Modern Tailwind UI forms)
- `views/dashboard.tsx` (Protected member dashboard)
- Automatically wires authentication routes into `routes/web.ts`

Run your migrations and test your new auth system:

```bash
npx birframework migrate
npm run dev
```

Navigate to `http://localhost:3000/login` to see your authentication UI in action.

---

## Password Hashing

Use `Hash` for scrypt password hashing. API tokens use a separate SHA-256 digest.

```ts
import { Hash } from 'birframework';

// Hash a plaintext password
const hashedPassword = await Hash.make('secret-password');

// Verify a plaintext password against the hash
const isValid = await Hash.check('secret-password', hashedPassword);
```

---

## Authentication Attempt

Authenticate incoming login credentials in a controller action:

```ts
import { Auth } from 'birframework';
import { User } from '../models/User.js';

export class AuthController {
  public async login(ctx) {
    const { email, password } = await ctx.validate({
      email: 'required|email',
      password: 'required',
    });

    const success = await Auth.attempt(ctx, { email, password }, User);

    if (!success) {
      return ctx.json({ error: 'Invalid credentials' }, 401);
    }

    return ctx.redirect('/dashboard');
  }

  public async logout(ctx) {
    await Auth.logout(ctx);
    return ctx.redirect('/');
  }
}
```

---

## Signed Cookies & Sessions

BirJS cryptographically signs cookies using `APP_KEY` from your `.env` file to prevent client-side tampering:

```ts
// Set a session value
ctx.session.set('cart_items', [101, 102]);

// Read a session value
const items = ctx.session.get('cart_items', []);

// Flash a message (persists only for the next request)
ctx.session.flash('status', 'Your profile has been updated!');
```

---

## API Tokens & Mobile Authentication (Sanctum Style)

BirJS includes first-class support for issuance and verification of API tokens, allowing you to authenticate SPAs, mobile apps, or third-party API clients using Bearer tokens.

### Adding Token Capabilities to Models

Equip your `User` model with the `HasApiTokens` mixin:

```typescript
import { Model, HasApiTokens } from 'birframework';

export class User extends HasApiTokens(Model) {
  // Model attributes & relationships
}
```

### Issuing Personal Access Tokens

Issue a token with specific fine-grained abilities:

```typescript
// Issue a token with full permissions:
const { plainTextToken } = await user.createToken('mobile-app');

// Or issue a token with scoped abilities and expiration:
const { plainTextToken } = await user.createToken('deploy-key', ['servers:read', 'servers:deploy'], new Date(Date.now() + 30 * 86400000));

return ctx.json({ token: plainTextToken });
```

Tokens are prefixed with `bir_pat_` and hashed with SHA-256 before storage in the `personal_access_tokens` table.

### Protecting Routes with Bearer Auth

Use the built-in `auth()` and `hasAbility()` middlewares to guard your API routes:

```typescript
import { Route, Auth, auth, hasAbility } from 'birframework';

// Authenticate any valid Bearer token:
Route.get('/api/user', async (ctx) => {
  return ctx.json(await Auth.user(ctx, User));
}).middleware(auth());

// Guard route by specific token ability:
Route.post('/api/servers/deploy', async (ctx) => {
  return ctx.json({ status: 'Deploying server...' });
}).middleware(auth(), hasAbility('servers:deploy'));
```

Clients authenticate simply by sending the standard `Authorization` header:

```http
Authorization: Bearer bir_pat_98f4b7a1e0c24d98a3b5c6e7f8a9b0c1...
```



## Persistent Session Drivers (`FileSessionStore` & `DatabaseSessionStore`)

By default, `sessionMiddleware()` uses an in-memory store. For production deployments across restarts or multiple workers, configure `file` or `database` persistence:

```ts
import { sessionMiddleware, FileSessionStore, DatabaseSessionStore, setSessionStore } from 'birframework';

// Option 1: Built-in File store
app.use(sessionMiddleware({ driver: 'file', storeDir: 'storage/framework/sessions' }));

// Option 2: Database store (_sessions table for SQLite, PostgreSQL, or MySQL)
app.use(sessionMiddleware({ driver: 'database' }));

// Option 3: Set globally
setSessionStore(new FileSessionStore('storage/framework/sessions'));
```


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/benchmarks

# Performance Measurement

The previous comparison measured BirJS 0.1.5. Those results do not describe the current TSX/JSX rendering stack. Measure the current application in production mode and record the framework version, runtime, hardware, response size, and database workload alongside each result.

## Build and start

```bash
npm ci
npm run build
NODE_ENV=production PORT=4001 npm start
```

Configure APP_KEY and database credentials before starting. Confirm the application reports the expected port and returns the intended page.

## Measure a representative endpoint

```bash
npx autocannon -c 10 -d 30 http://127.0.0.1:4001/
```

Run a warm-up first and repeat the measurement. Record throughput, latency percentiles, error counts, and response bytes. Measure JSON endpoints and rendered pages separately. Include authentication and database queries when those are part of the real workload.

Comparisons require the same host, concurrency, duration, response content, and production setup. Publish raw outputs and exact configuration with any performance claim.


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/cache

# Cache System

BirJS provides an expressive, unified API for various caching backends. Because Node.js runs in persistent V8 memory (unlike traditional PHP-FPM), in-memory caching operates at low latency out of the box with zero external infrastructure.

---

## Configuration & Drivers

BirJS supports three built-in cache drivers:

| Driver | Description | Persistence |
|---|---|---|
| `memory` | In-memory key-value store with TTL (Default) | In-process V8 RAM (Process-local) |
| `redis` | Redis server, configured with `REDIS_URL` | Shared across processes |
| `file` | Serialized JSON files in `storage/cache/` | Survives server restarts |

Configure your default driver via `.env`:

```env
CACHE_STORE=memory
# or CACHE_STORE=file
```

---

## Basic Usage

Import the `Cache` facade:

```ts
import { Cache } from 'birframework';
```

### Storing Items

Store an item with an optional TTL in seconds (omit or pass `0` to keep forever):

```ts
// Store for 10 minutes (600 seconds)
await Cache.put('site_settings', { theme: 'dark', notifications: true }, 600);

// Store indefinitely
await Cache.put('app_version', '1.0.0');
```

### Retrieving Items

```ts
const settings = await Cache.get('site_settings');

// With fallback default value
const theme = await Cache.get('user_theme', 'light');
```

### Checking Existence

```ts
if (await Cache.has('site_settings')) {
  // Key exists and has not expired
}
```

---

## The `remember` Method

The crown jewel of caching ergonomics: retrieves an item from cache if it exists, or executes the callback, stores the result for the given TTL, and returns it.

```ts
import { Cache, Route, type Context } from 'birframework';
import { Post } from '../app/models/Post.js';

Route.get('/api/posts/popular', async (ctx: Context) => {
  const posts = await Cache.remember('popular_posts', 300, async () => {
    // Heavy database query only runs once every 5 minutes
    return await Post.where('views', '>', 1000)
      .orderBy('views', 'desc')
      .limit(10)
      .get();
  });

  return ctx.json(posts);
});
```

To remember an item forever:

```ts
const categories = await Cache.rememberForever('categories', async () => {
  return await Category.all();
});
```

---

## Counters & Pull

### Incrementing and Decrementing

```ts
// Increment by 1
await Cache.increment('page_views');

// Increment by custom amount
await Cache.increment('credits', 10);

// Decrement
await Cache.decrement('credits', 5);
```

### Pull (Retrieve & Delete)

Retrieve an item and immediately remove it from cache:

```ts
const token = await Cache.pull('one_time_token');
```

### Removing Items & Flushing

```ts
// Remove a single key
await Cache.forget('site_settings');

// Clear the entire cache
await Cache.flush();
```

---

## Multi-Store Switching

You can switch between different cache stores on the fly:

```ts
// Store in file cache (persisted across restarts)
await Cache.store('file').put('license_key', 'valid', 86400);

// Retrieve from in-memory cache
const memoryVal = await Cache.store('memory').get('session_id');
```

Redis requires `npm install ioredis` and a running Redis server. File and memory stores have different concurrency guarantees. Treat read-modify-write counters according to the selected driver.


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/cli

# CLI Command Reference

BirJS provides an artisan-style command-line tool `bir` for code generation, migrations, worker daemons, and project management.

---

## Project Scaffolding

```bash
# Interactive new project wizard
npx birframework new <project-name>

# Headless options
npx birframework new <project-name> --ts --tailwind
npx birframework new <project-name> --js --css
```

---

## Code Generators (`make:*`)

Generate boilerplate code following framework architectural patterns:

| Command | Description | Output Location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bir make:controller <Name>` | Creates a controller class | `app/controllers/<Name>.ts` |
| `bir make:model <Name>` | Creates an Active Record Model (`-m`, `-c`, `-r`, `-f`, `-s`, `--all`) | `app/models/<Name>.ts` |
| `bir make:component <Name>` | Creates a Preact TSX/JSX component | `views/components/` |
| `bir make:view <Name>` | Creates a Preact TSX/JSX view | `views/pages/` for Inertia, otherwise `views/` |
| `bir make:provider <Name>` | Creates a Service Provider | `app/providers/<Name>.ts` |
| `bir make:migration <Name>` | Creates a timestamped migration | `database/migrations/<timestamp>_<Name>.ts` |
| `bir make:middleware <Name>` | Creates a custom middleware | `app/middleware/<Name>.ts` |
| `bir make:job <Name>` | Creates an asynchronous queue job | `app/jobs/<Name>.ts` |
| `bir make:mail <Name>` | Creates a mailable email class | `app/mail/<Name>.ts` |
| `bir make:seeder <Name>` | Creates a database seeder class | `database/seeders/<Name>.ts` |
| `bir make:factory <Name>` | Creates a model factory with Faker | `database/factories/<Name>.ts` |
| `bir make:event <Name>` | Creates an event class | `app/events/<Name>.ts` |
| `bir make:listener <Name> [--event]` | Creates an event listener class | `app/listeners/<Name>.ts` |
| `bir make:request <Name>` | Creates a Form Request class | `app/requests/<Name>.ts` |
| `bir make:auth` | Scaffolds complete Breeze-style auth | Models, Controllers, Views, Migrations |
| `bir make:vercel` | Scaffolds zero-config Vercel Serverless deployment | `vercel.json`, `api/index.js` |

---

## Database & Migrations

```bash
# Run all outstanding migrations
bir migrate

# Roll back the most recent migration batch
bir migrate:rollback

# Drop all tables and re-run all migrations
bir migrate:fresh

# Seed the database with test records
bir db:seed
```

---

## Daemons & Development

```bash
# Start full-stack multi-process dev dashboard (Server, Queue, Logs, Vite)
bir dev

# Live real-time application log stream (tailing storage/logs/bir.log)
bir pail

# Start development server with hot-reload
bir serve

# Launch interactive REPL console with auto-loaded models
bir tinker

# Run automated test suites
bir test

# List all registered routes and handlers
bir route:list

# Start background queue processing worker
bir queue:work

# Inspect, retry, or flush failed background jobs
bir queue:failed
bir queue:retry all
bir queue:flush

# Put application into maintenance mode (503) or bring it back up
bir down --message="Upgrading database" --retry=60
bir up

# Generate a secure APP_KEY in .env (used by Crypt & SignedUrl)
bir key:generate

# Start scheduler daemon (tasks must already be registered in that process)
bir schedule:work

# Scaffold authentication controllers and views
bir make:auth

# Generate Vercel Serverless deployment config (vercel.json + api/index.js)
bir make:vercel
```

---

## Serverless & Deployment

New projects created with `npx birframework new` come pre-configured for Vercel Serverless. If you are upgrading an existing project or regenerating deployment files, run:

```bash
bir make:vercel
```

This generates:
- `vercel.json` — configures `npm run build --if-present`, `public` output directory, included static/docs bundles, and rewrites to `/api/index.js`.
- `api/index.js` — mounts `compress()`, `serveStatic({ publicDir: 'public' })`, `Inertia.middleware()`, and exports `app.serverless()`.

> `app.serverless()` also works on AWS Lambda and Netlify-compatible Node runtimes (additional platform generators such as Netlify are planned).


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/components

# Components

Build reusable interface elements as Preact functions in `views/components/`. Use props for data, children for nested content, and hooks for browser interaction in hydrated Inertia pages.

## Generate a component

```bash
npx bir make:component Card
```

The generator creates `views/components/Card.tsx` in a TypeScript project or `Card.jsx` in a JavaScript project.

## Props and children

```tsx
import type { ComponentChildren } from 'preact';

export function Card({ title, children }: {
  title: string;
  children?: ComponentChildren;
}) {
  return <section class="rounded-lg border p-6">
    <h2>{title}</h2>
    {children}
  </section>;
}
```

Import the component into a page and compose it with other components.

```tsx
import { Card } from '../components/Card';

export default function Welcome() {
  return <Card title="Your project"><p>Ready to build.</p></Card>;
}
```

## Interactive components

```tsx
import { useState } from 'preact/hooks';

export function Toggle() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return <div>
    <button type="button" aria-expanded={open} onClick={() => setOpen(!open)}>
      Details
    </button>
    {open && <p>More information about this item.</p>}
  </div>;
}
```

Use this component in a hydrated Inertia page. Browser event handlers require a client bundle. Server-only rendering produces HTML without activating handlers.

## Organizing components

Group related components in subdirectories and keep complete screens in `views/pages/`. Share state through props and callbacks. Keep browser-only APIs inside event handlers or effects so server rendering can run without `window` or `document`.


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/configuration

# Configuration and Environment

BirJS loads a root `.env` file on framework import. Existing process environment values take precedence. Environment values are strings, so convert numbers and booleans explicitly.

```ini
NODE_ENV=development
PORT=3000
DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_DATABASE=storage/database.sqlite
CACHE_STORE=memory
```

Generate a private application key with `npx bir key:generate`.

## Reading values

```ts
const port = Number(process.env.PORT) || 3000;
const debug = process.env.APP_DEBUG === 'true';
const name = process.env.APP_NAME || 'My App';
```

## Application configuration

`Config` provides a process-local configuration store. Import your configuration files explicitly and register their values during bootstrap. The database driver reads DB_* environment variables directly.

```ts
import { Config, config } from 'birframework';

Config.set('app.name', process.env.APP_NAME || 'My App');
const name = config<string>('app.name');
```

Application registers default memory sessions and security headers. Configure persistent sessions and additional middleware explicitly. An environment variable alone does not install middleware. Vite can discover its listening address using `birVite()`. See [Development server](/docs/dev-server).


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/controllers

# Controllers & Actions

Controllers centralize HTTP request handling logic into dedicated classes instead of writing bloated inline route closures.

---

## Creating a Controller

Create a controller manually in `app/controllers/` or generate one with the CLI:

```bash
npx birframework make:controller UserController
```

Example controller class:

```ts
// app/controllers/UserController.ts
import type { Context } from 'birframework';
import { User } from '../models/User.ts';

export class UserController {
  /**
   * Display a listing of users.
   */
  public async index(ctx: Context) {
    const users = await User.query().orderBy('created_at', 'DESC').get();
    return ctx.render('users/index', { users });
  }

  /**
   * Display a specific user.
   */
  public async show(ctx: Context) {
    const user = await User.find(ctx.params.id);
    if (!user) {
      return ctx.json({ error: 'User not found' }, 404);
    }
    return ctx.json(user);
  }

  /**
   * Store a newly created user in storage.
   */
  public async store(ctx: Context) {
    const validated = await ctx.validate({
      name: 'required|min:3',
      email: 'required|email|unique:users,email',
    });

    const user = await User.create(validated);
    return ctx.json(user, 201);
  }
}
```

---

## Binding Controllers to Routes

Pass an instance or class action to your route definition:

```ts
// routes/web.ts
import { Route } from 'birframework';
import { UserController } from '../app/controllers/UserController.ts';

const userCtrl = new UserController();

Route.get('/users', (ctx) => userCtrl.index(ctx));
Route.get('/users/:id', (ctx) => userCtrl.show(ctx));
Route.post('/users', (ctx) => userCtrl.store(ctx));
```

---

## Context Helpers

The `Context` object passed to controller actions contains rich utility methods:

- `ctx.params`: Route parameters (`/users/:id` -> `ctx.params.id`)
- `ctx.query`: URL query string parameters (`?page=2` -> `ctx.query.page`)
- `await ctx.body()`: Parsed request payload (JSON or Form URL-encoded)
- `ctx.json(data, status?)`: Return JSON response
- `ctx.render(view, data?)`: Render a named Preact TSX/JSX view
- `ctx.redirect(url, status?)`: HTTP redirect
- `ctx.session`: Optional session store, available after sessionMiddleware() (get, set, flash)


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/database

# Multi-Driver Database Engine

BirJS includes a unified database connection layer supporting SQLite, PostgreSQL, and MySQL.

---

## Configuration

The default connection reads environment variables directly.

```ini
DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_DATABASE=storage/database.sqlite
```

For PostgreSQL use `DB_CONNECTION=postgres`, port 5432 and install `pg`. For MySQL use `DB_CONNECTION=mysql`, port 3306 and install `mysql2`. Both read `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_DATABASE`, `DB_USERNAME`, and `DB_PASSWORD`, or `DATABASE_URL`.

```bash
npm install pg
# For MySQL instead:
# npm install mysql2
```

An explicit connection uses `new DatabaseConnection({ driver, host, port, database, user, password })`. The option is `user`, while the environment variable is `DB_USERNAME`.

## Zero-Dependency SQLite

BirJS uses Node's built-in `node:sqlite` engine when running on Node.js 22+. No external binary downloads, C++ node-gyp compilers, or heavy native dependencies are required.

---

## Raw Queries & Fluent Query Builder

Execute raw parameterized SQL queries or use the fluent query builder:

```ts
import { DB } from 'birframework';

// Raw parameterized query
const activeUsers = await DB.raw(
  'SELECT * FROM users WHERE status = ? AND age >= ?',
  ['active', 21]
);

// Fluent query builder
const count = await DB.table('orders')
  .where('status', 'completed')
  .count();

// Transactions
await DB.transaction(async () => {
  await DB.table('accounts').where('id', 1).decrement('balance', 100);
  await DB.table('accounts').where('id', 2).increment('balance', 100);
});
```


## Pessimistic Row Locking (`forUpdate`)

For concurrent-safe balance, inventory, or invoice updates on PostgreSQL and MySQL, chain `.forUpdate()` inside a transaction:

```ts
await DB.transaction(async () => {
  const wallet = await DB.table('wallets')
    .where('user_id', userId)
    .forUpdate()
    .first();
  // Safe to update wallet balance
});
```

*(On SQLite, `.forUpdate()` is a safe no-op.)*


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/dev-server

# Development Dashboard & Vite HMR

BirJS features a unified development environment designed to run your entire application stack in a single terminal session. Rather than opening separate terminal tabs for your web server, queue worker, asset compiler, and log watcher, BirJS coordinates all four services concurrently.

---

## The 4-Service Dev Dashboard

When you start your project with:

```bash
npm run dev
# or via CLI
npx bir dev
```

The generated Inertia profile boots four dedicated background processes using high-contrast terminal colors:

```text
[server] > npx tsx watch app.ts
[queue]  > npx bir queue:work
[logs]   > npx bir pail
[vite]   > vite
```

### Process Roles

| Service | Color | Command | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`server`** | `#00f5d4` (Teal) | `npx tsx watch app.ts` | The core HTTP server with Hot Reload on code changes. |
| **`queue`** | `#7209b7` (Purple) | `npx bir queue:work` | Consumes asynchronous background jobs. Run scheduled tasks with `bir schedule:work`. |
| **`logs`** | `#f72585` (Pink) | `npx bir pail` | Real-time structured log streaming with ANSI category badges. |
| **`vite`** | `#ffb703` (Amber) | `vite` | Vite dev server compiling client CSS, TypeScript, and Preact + Inertia `.tsx` pages. |

---

## Automatic Port Switching

The HTTP server retries the next port when its requested port is occupied. Vite handles its own port fallback when strictPort is false. Register birVite() so rendered asset URLs follow the port selected by Vite.

```text
➜ Port 3000 is in use, trying 3001 instead...
✔ Automatically switched to available port: http://localhost:3001
[app] BirJS ready at http://localhost:3001
```

You never need to manually hunt down and kill PID processes just to run your app.

---

## Tailwind CSS v4 Integration

BirJS fully supports Tailwind CSS v4. Because BirJS views (`.tsx` / `.jsx` pages and components) live under `views/`, the stylesheet uses `@source` scanning directives.

In `resources/css/app.css`:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";

@source "../../views";
@source "../../app";
```

These directives instruct Tailwind v4 to continuously inspect your controller returns, JSX components, and view templates for utility classes.

---

## Vite Backend Template Hot Reloading

When editing server-side templates or views, standard frontend bundlers typically do not trigger browser reloads. BirJS includes a custom watcher plugin inside `vite.config.js`:

```js
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import { birVite } from 'birframework';
import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    birVite(),
    tailwindcss(),
    {
      name: 'bir-watch-views',
      handleHotUpdate({ file, server }) {
        if (file.includes('/views/') || file.includes('/app/')) {
          server.ws.send({
            type: 'full-reload',
            path: '*',
          });
        }
      },
    },
  ],
  server: {
    cors: true,
  },
});
```

Whenever you modify any file inside `views/` or `app/`, the browser automatically performs a full-reload with the latest rendered markup and compiled Tailwind utility styles.


## Vite port discovery

Register `birVite()` from `birframework` in your Vite plugins. The plugin writes the actual development server address to `storage/framework/vite.json`. Both Inertia and server-rendered Vite tags read this address, including when port 5173 is occupied and Vite selects another port.

```js
import { birVite } from 'birframework';

// In your existing Vite configuration:
// plugins: [birVite(), ...otherPlugins]
```

Allow port fallback with `strictPort: false` and omit a fixed `server.origin`. An explicit `VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL` overrides discovery, which is useful behind a development proxy. Production continues to use the build manifest.


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/directory-structure

# Directory Structure

The generated structure depends on language and rendering profile. The following tree combines the default Inertia directories with optional application directories. Create and import optional configuration and route files explicitly.

---

## Directory Overview

```
my-bir-app/
├── app/
│   ├── controllers/       # HTTP Request Handlers
│   ├── models/            # Active Record ORM Models
│   ├── middleware/        # HTTP Middleware Pipeline
│   ├── jobs/              # Asynchronous Queue Jobs
│   ├── mail/              # Mailable Email Classes
│   └── providers/         # Optional service providers
├── config/                # Optional, explicitly imported
│   ├── app.ts             # App-wide Configuration
│   ├── database.ts        # Database Connections & Drivers
│   └── queue.ts           # Queue Driver Settings
├── database/
│   ├── migrations/        # Incremental Schema Migrations
│   └── seeders/           # Database Test Seeders
├── public/                # Static Assets (Images, Favicons, CSS)
├── routes/
│   ├── web.ts             # Browser Web Routes (HTML Views)
│   └── api.ts             # Optional, import it from bootstrap
├── views/
│   ├── layouts/           # Shared TSX/JSX layouts
│   ├── components/        # Reusable Preact components
│   └── pages/
│       └── Welcome.tsx   # Inertia page
├── storage/               # File Storage, Logs, and SQLite DBs
├── .env                   # Local Environment Variables
├── app.ts                 # Application Bootstrap Entrypoint
└── package.json
```

---

## Key Directories Explained

### `app/controllers/`
Houses your HTTP controllers. Controllers group related request handling logic, interact with models, and return JSON responses or rendered Preact views.

### `app/models/`
Defines your database models extending `Model`. Each model provides active record query building, relationships, validation, and serialization.

### `database/migrations/`
Version-controlled database schema changes. Migrations let you incrementally alter tables and roll back changes across environments.

### `views/`
Holds Preact TSX/JSX views. Inertia pages live in `views/pages/`, shared layouts in `views/layouts/`, and reusable components in `views/components/`.

### `storage/`
Stores uploaded files, temporary cache, job locks, and default SQLite databases (`storage/database.sqlite`).


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/error-handling

# Error Handling & Ignition Debug Screen

BirJS includes a built-in, zero-config interactive error handling engine inspired by **Laravel Ignition** and **Next.js Error Overlay**.

---

## Interactive Ignition Debug Screen

In development (`NODE_ENV !== 'production'`), when an unhandled exception occurs during a browser request, BirJS intercepts the failure and presents a sleek, interactive debug screen:

### Key Features
1. **Source Code Preview**: Automatically inspects the call stack, locates the exact application file and line number, and renders the code snippet with the faulting line highlighted in red.
2. **Filtered Stack Trace**: Distinguishes your application frames from external vendor / `node_modules` frames so you can focus on your code immediately.
3. **Context Tabs**:
   - **Request**: HTTP Method, URL, Path, and incoming request headers.
   - **Query & Body**: Parsed query parameters and POST payloads.
   - **Session**: Active session key-value pairs.
   - **Environment**: Node.js version, platform, OS architecture, and process uptime.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ BirJS development  •  GET /posts/my-slug  •  500 ERR │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined         │
│ app/controllers/PostController.ts:42                   │
│                                                        │
│  40 │  const slug = ctx.params.slug;                   │
│  41 │  const post = await Post.firstWhere('slug', slug);│
│ >42 │  return ctx.render('posts/show', { post });      │
│  43 │}                                                 │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## API & JSON Error Responses

If an exception occurs during an API request (`Accept: application/json` or paths starting with `/api`), BirJS automatically formats the error as structured JSON:

```json
{
  "error": "TypeError",
  "message": "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'title')",
  "file": "app/controllers/PostController.ts",
  "line": 42,
  "stack": "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined..."
}
```

---

## Production Security (`NODE_ENV=production`)

In production environments, detailed stack traces, file paths, and code snippets are **strictly masked** to protect sensitive infrastructure data:

- **Browser Requests**: Renders `views/errors/500.tsx` if present in your project, or falls back to BirJS's minimal, production-safe 500 error page.
- **API Requests**: Returns `{ "error": "Internal Server Error", "message": "Server Error" }` with HTTP status `500`.

---

## Smart 404 Not Found Handling

When an incoming request matches no registered route:

1. **Browser Requests (`text/html`)**:
   - Automatically searches for `views/errors/404.tsx`.
   - If not found, renders BirJS's built-in dark-themed 404 page displaying the requested path and a link back to the homepage.
2. **API Requests (`application/json` or `/api/*`)**:
   - Responds with standard 404 JSON:
   ```json
   {
     "error": "Not Found",
     "message": "Route [GET /unknown-path] not found.",
     "path": "/unknown-path",
     "method": "GET"
   }
   ```


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/events

# Events & Listeners

BirJS provides an asynchronous, type-safe **Event** and **Listener** system. Events serve as a great way to decouple various aspects of your application, since a single event can have multiple listeners that don't depend on each other.

---

## 1. Scaffolding Events & Listeners

Generate an event and a corresponding listener using the CLI:

```bash
npx birframework make:event UserRegistered
npx birframework make:listener SendWelcomeEmail --event UserRegistered
```

### Event Definition (`app/events/UserRegistered.ts`)

```typescript
import { User } from '../models/User.js';

export class UserRegistered {
  constructor(public user: User) {}
}

export default UserRegistered;
```

### Listener Definition (`app/listeners/SendWelcomeEmail.ts`)

```typescript
import { UserRegistered } from '../events/UserRegistered.js';
import { Mail } from 'birframework';

export class SendWelcomeEmail {
  public async handle(event: UserRegistered): Promise<void> {
    await Mail.to(event.user.email).raw('<p>Thanks for joining us.</p>', { subject: 'Welcome to BirJS!' });
  }
}

export default SendWelcomeEmail;
```

---

## 2. Registering Listeners

Register listeners anywhere in your application boot lifecycle (such as `app.ts` or a service provider):

```typescript
import { Event } from 'birframework';
import { UserRegistered } from './events/UserRegistered.js';
import { SendWelcomeEmail } from './listeners/SendWelcomeEmail.js';

// Register class listener
Event.listen(UserRegistered, SendWelcomeEmail);

// Or register an inline callback function
Event.listen(UserRegistered, async (event) => {
  console.log(`User created with ID: ${event.user.id}`);
});

// Or use string events with wildcards
Event.listen('order.*', (data) => {
  console.log('Order event caught:', data);
});
```

---

## 3. Dispatching Events

Dispatch events using the `Event.dispatch()` facade:

```typescript
import { Event } from 'birframework';
import { UserRegistered } from './events/UserRegistered.js';

// Dispatch a class event
const user = await User.create({ name: 'John Doe', email: 'john@example.com' });
await Event.dispatch(new UserRegistered(user));

// Dispatch a named string event with payload
await Event.dispatch('order.completed', { orderId: 452, amount: 99.0 });
```

### Stopping Early with `until`

Use `Event.until()` to stop dispatching as soon as the first listener returns a non-null result:

```typescript
const result = await Event.until('payment.verify', { cardToken: 'tok_123' });
if (result?.approved) {
  // Process approved payment
}
```

---

## 4. Testing with `Event.fake()`

When writing automated tests, you often want to verify that an event was fired without actually triggering heavy listeners (like sending emails or external webhooks). BirJS includes testing utilities inspired by Laravel:

```typescript
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert';
import { Event } from 'birframework';
import { UserRegistered } from '../app/events/UserRegistered.js';

test('registering a user dispatches UserRegistered event', async () => {
  // 1. Fake the event dispatcher
  Event.fake();

  // 2. Perform the action
  await registerUserAction({ name: 'Jane', email: 'jane@example.com' });

  // 3. Assert the event was dispatched
  Event.assertDispatched(UserRegistered);

  // 4. Assert with callback payload inspection
  Event.assertDispatched(UserRegistered, (event) => {
    return event.user.email === 'jane@example.com';
  });

  // 5. Assert unexpected event was not dispatched
  Event.assertNotDispatched('user.deleted');

  // 6. Restore real dispatching
  Event.restore();
});
```

---

## 5. Real-Time Broadcasting & WebSockets

BirJS includes a built-in WebSocket broadcasting server that lets you push live events to connected browsers without external services:

### Broadcasting an Event

Broadcast from anywhere in your controllers, jobs, or listeners:

```typescript
import { Broadcast } from 'birframework';

// Public channel broadcast:
Broadcast.to('orders').emit('OrderCreated', {
  orderId: 101,
  total: 250.00,
  customer: 'Jane Doe'
});
```

### Authorizing Private Channels

Secure private channels using channel authorization rules:

```typescript
// Authorize access to user-specific private channel:
Broadcast.channel('private-user.{id}', (client, params) => {
  return String(client.user?.id) === params?.id;
});
```

### Client-Side Integration

In your client-side components or browser modules, connect using the WebSocket protocol:

```javascript
const protocol = location.protocol === 'https:' ? 'wss:' : 'ws:';
const ws = new WebSocket(`${protocol}//${location.host}/ws`);
ws.onopen = () => ws.send(JSON.stringify({ event: 'subscribe', channel: 'orders' }));

ws.onmessage = (event) => {
  const { channel, event: eventName, data } = JSON.parse(event.data);
  if (channel === 'orders' && eventName === 'OrderCreated') {
    console.log('New order received:', data);
  }
};
```



Source: https://birjs.com/docs/factories

# Model Factories & Database Seeding

When developing applications and writing automated tests, generating realistic test data quickly is essential. BirJS provides a built-in **Factory** system and lightweight **Faker** utility, completely eliminating the need for bulky third-party mock libraries.

---

## 1. Creating a Factory

Scaffold a new factory using the BirJS CLI:

```bash
npx birframework make:factory UserFactory
```

This generates `database/factories/UserFactory.ts`:

```typescript
import { Factory, type Faker } from 'birframework';
import { User } from '../../app/models/User.js';

export const UserFactory = Factory.define(User, (faker: Faker) => ({
  name: faker.name(),
  email: faker.email(),
  role: 'member',
  created_at: new Date(),
  updated_at: new Date(),
}));

export default UserFactory;
```

---

## 2. The Built-in Faker Utility

The `Faker` generator provides common fake data generators with zero external dependencies:

```typescript
faker.name()               // "Jane Miller"
faker.email('example.com') // "jane.miller84@example.com"
faker.number(10, 100)      // 42
faker.boolean()            // true / false
faker.uuid()               // "a3f5c1d2e8b4..."
faker.word()               // "lorem"
faker.sentence()           // "Quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris."
faker.paragraph()          // Full multi-sentence paragraph
faker.pick(['a', 'b'])     // Random element from array
```

---

## 3. Using Factories

### Generating In-Memory Attributes (`raw`)

Generate plain JavaScript objects without touching the database:

```typescript
const attributes = UserFactory.raw({ role: 'admin' });
// { name: "Jane Miller", email: "...", role: "admin", ... }
```

### Creating In-Memory Model Instances (`make`)

Instantiate unpersisted `Model` instances:

```typescript
const user = UserFactory.make({ role: 'admin' });
console.log(user.name); // Access model properties directly
```

### Persisting to the Database (`create`)

Save the generated model directly to your configured SQL database (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL):

```typescript
const user = await UserFactory.create();
console.log(user.id); // Primary key assigned by database
```

### Generating Multiple Records (`count`)

Combine `.count()` with `.make()` or `.create()`:

```typescript
// Create 20 users in memory
const users = UserFactory.count(20).make();

// Insert 50 users into the database
const persistedUsers = await UserFactory.count(50).create();
```

---

## 4. Factory States

Define reusable state modifications for specific scenarios (e.g. VIP customers, unverified emails, admins):

```typescript
export const UserFactory = Factory.define(User, (faker) => ({
  name: faker.name(),
  email: faker.email(),
  role: 'member',
  email_verified: true,
}));

// Usage:
const admin = await UserFactory.state({ role: 'admin' }).create();
const unverifiedUsers = await UserFactory.state({ email_verified: false }).count(5).create();
```

---

## 5. Database Seeders

BirJS seeders allow you to populate your database with initial data or realistic mock records:

```bash
npx birframework make:seeder DatabaseSeeder
```

In `database/seeders/DatabaseSeeder.ts`:

```typescript
import { Seeder } from 'birframework';
import { UserFactory } from '../factories/UserFactory.js';

export class DatabaseSeeder extends Seeder {
  public async run(): Promise<void> {
    // Seed 1 default superadmin
    await UserFactory.create({
      name: 'Super Admin',
      email: 'admin@birjs.com',
      role: 'admin',
    });

    // Seed 50 test users
    await UserFactory.count(50).create();
  }
}

export default DatabaseSeeder;
```

Run seeders at any time with:

```bash
npx birframework db:seed
```


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/inertia

# Unified Preact + Inertia + SSR

BirJS combines Laravel-style server routing and controllers with a single unified **Preact + Inertia + SSR** frontend stack. Write all your pages and interactive UI using one consistent TSX standard (`preact`) with full `useState`, `useEffect`, and `onClick` support — while preserving instant Server-Side Rendering (SSR) on initial page load.

---

## How It Works

1. **First Page Load (SEO + Zero Flicker):**
   When a user or search engine visits `/`, `ctx.inertia('Welcome', props)` renders `views/pages/Welcome.tsx` on the server via `preact-render-to-string`, embeds the serialized props in `<div id="app" data-page="...">`, and Preact hydrates it in the browser.
2. **SPA Transitions (`<Link>` & `router`):**
   Clicking `<Link href="/invoices">` sends a lightweight fetch with `X-Bir-Inertia: true`. BirJS returns only `{ component, props, url }` as JSON, swapping the active page without a full page reload — preserving shared UI when implemented through persistent layouts.

---

## Returning Inertia Pages from Controllers

```ts
// app/controllers/InvoiceController.ts
import type { Context } from 'birframework';
import { Invoice } from '../models/Invoice.js';

export class InvoiceController {
  public async index(ctx: Context) {
    const invoices = await Invoice.all();
    // Resolves views/pages/Invoices/Index.tsx
    return ctx.inertia('Invoices/Index', { invoices });
  }
}
```

---

## Writing Pages & Persistent Layouts

```tsx
// views/pages/Invoices/Index.tsx
import { useState } from 'preact/hooks';
import { Link, router, usePage } from '../../../../resources/js/bir-inertia';

export default function Index({ invoices }: { invoices: any[] }) {
  const { props } = usePage<{ flash?: { success?: string } }>();
  const [modalOpen, setModalOpen] = useState(false);

  return (
    <div className="min-h-screen bg-[#09090b] text-white p-8">
      <nav className="flex items-center justify-between mb-8">
        <Link href="/" className="text-sm text-zinc-400 hover:text-white">Home</Link>
        <button onClick={() => setModalOpen(true)} className="px-3 py-1.5 rounded bg-white text-black text-xs font-medium">
          New Invoice
        </button>
      </nav>

      {props.flash?.success && (
        <div className="mb-4 p-3 rounded bg-emerald-500/10 text-emerald-400 text-xs">{props.flash.success}</div>
      )}

      <h1 className="text-2xl font-bold">Invoices ({invoices.length})</h1>

      {modalOpen && (
        <div className="fixed inset-0 bg-black/70 flex items-center justify-center">
          <div className="bg-zinc-950 border border-zinc-800 rounded-xl p-6">
            <h2 className="text-sm font-semibold">Create Invoice</h2>
            <button onClick={() => { router.post('/invoices', { amount: 100 }); setModalOpen(false); }}>
              Submit
            </button>
          </div>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

---

## Sharing Global Props (`Inertia.share`)

Share authenticated user state or global settings across every page automatically:

```ts
import { Inertia, Auth } from 'birframework';

Inertia.share('auth', async (ctx) => ({
  user: await Auth.user(ctx),
}));
```

Session flash messages (`success`, `error`, `errors`) are shared automatically on `props.flash`.

---

## External / Full Redirects (`Inertia.location`)

```ts
import { Inertia } from 'birframework';

Inertia.location(ctx, '/login'); // Sends 409 X-Bir-Inertia-Location for SPA requests
```


## Persistent Layouts (`Page.layout`)

To keep shared UI (such as sidebars, audio players, or navigation state) mounted across page visits, attach a `layout` callback to your page component:

```tsx
import { AppLayout } from '../layouts/AppLayout';

export default function Dashboard({ stats }) {
  return <div>...</div>;
}

Dashboard.layout = (page) => <AppLayout>{page}</AppLayout>;
```

## Forms & File Uploads (`useForm`)

Use `useForm` to manage form state, loading states, automatic `FormData` file serialization, and 422 validation errors:

```tsx
import { useForm } from '../../resources/js/bir-inertia';

function UploadForm() {
const { data, setData, post, processing, errors, wasSuccessful } = useForm({
  title: '',
  cover: null as File | null,
});

const submit = (e: Event) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  post('/tracks', { preserveScroll: true });
};
return <form onSubmit={submit}>
  <input value={data.title} onInput={(e) => setData('title', e.currentTarget.value)} />
  <button disabled={processing}>Save</button>
</form>;
}
```

## Scroll Preservation, `<Head>`, & Navigation State

- **Scroll Preservation:** Pass `preserveScroll: true` to `<Link href="/..." preserveScroll />` or `router.visit(url, { preserveScroll: true })`.
- **Dynamic Document Head:** Use `<Head title="My Page" description="..." canonical="https://..." />` inside pages to sync `<title>`, `description`, `og:title`, `og:description`, and `canonical` on client navigation.
- **Progress Indicator:** `AppShell` renders a top `#bir-progress-bar` automatically during visits, and `useNavigation()` exposes `{ navigating }`.

## Server-Side SSR SEO & Meta Tags

Pass `lang`, `title`, `description`, `canonical`, and `meta` (`robots`, `og`, `twitter`, `tags`) directly from your controller:

```ts
await ctx.inertia('TldDetail', { tld: 'com' }, {
  lang: 'tr',
  title: '.com Domain Prices',
  description: 'Compare .com registration and renewal prices.',
  canonical: 'https://example.com/tld/com',
  meta: {
    robots: 'index, follow',
    og: { image: 'https://example.com/og.png', siteName: 'tlds' },
    twitter: { card: 'summary_large_image' },
  },
});
```


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/installation

# Installation Guide

Get up and running with BirJS in seconds using the official interactive CLI scaffolder.

---

## System Requirements

Before creating your first project, ensure your environment satisfies the following prerequisites:

- **Node.js**: `v22.5.0` or higher
- **NPM**: `v9.0.0` or higher, or `pnpm` / `yarn`
- **Operating System**: macOS, Linux, or Windows (WSL recommended)

---

## Quickstart Scaffolding

Run `npx birframework new` directly in your terminal to bootstrap a fresh application:

```bash
npx birframework new my-bir-app
```

The interactive installer displays the recommended modern stack (**TypeScript (.ts/.tsx) + Tailwind CSS v4 + Unified Preact & Inertia + Vite**):
- Press **Enter** to install immediately with the recommended defaults.
- Or type **`c`** to customize Language (`TypeScript` / `JavaScript`), Styling (`Tailwind` / `Pure CSS`), or rendering profile (`Inertia` / `Server-rendered`).

Alternatively, pass flags directly for headless CI/CD automation:

```bash
# Default full-stack TypeScript + Tailwind v4 + Preact + Inertia + Vite
npx birframework new my-app --ts --tailwind --inertia

# Minimal MPA without Vite
npx birframework new my-app --ts --css --server-rendered
```

---

## Starting the Development Server

Navigate into your newly scaffolded application and launch the dev server:

```bash
cd my-bir-app
npm install
npm run dev
```

The application will start on `http://localhost:3000`.

> **Port Auto-Increment**: If port `3000` is already in use by another service on your machine, BirJS automatically detects `EADDRINUSE` and gracefully switches to the next available port (`3001`, `3002`, etc.) without crashing.

---

## Available Scripts

| Script | Command | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | `concurrently ...` | Boots the 4-service dev suite (`server`, `queue`, `logs`, `vite`) |
| `npm run dev:server` | `npx tsx watch app.ts` | Runs the core HTTP server with Hot Reload and auto port increment |
| `npm run dev:queue` | `npx bir queue:work` | Consumes asynchronous jobs (run scheduling separately with `bir schedule:work`) |
| `npm run dev:logs` | `npx bir pail` | Streams real-time colorized logs directly in your terminal |
| `npm run dev:vite` | `vite` | Starts Vite HMR and auto-reload watcher for views and templates |
| `npm run build` | `vite build` | Compiles production assets to `public/build` with manifest |
| `npm start` | `npx tsx app.ts` | Boots the production application server |

---

## Deploying to Vercel

Every project scaffolded with `npx birframework new` includes `vercel.json` and `api/index.js` out of the box, so you can deploy immediately by running `vercel` or pushing to GitHub.

If you need to add or regenerate Vercel Serverless configuration in an existing project, run:

```bash
npx bir make:vercel
```

This wires up `app.serverless()` with `compress()`, `serveStatic({ publicDir: 'public' })`, and `Inertia.middleware()`. Set a random `APP_KEY` in your Vercel Project Environment Variables for production deployments.


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/jsx

# TSX and JSX

BirJS uses Preact for TSX and JSX views. TypeScript projects use `.tsx` components and JavaScript projects use `.jsx` components.

Use `ctx.inertia()` with `views/pages/` for hydrated pages and client navigation. Use `ctx.render()` with named views for server-rendered HTML.

See [Views](/docs/views), [Components](/docs/components), and [Inertia](/docs/inertia) for setup and examples.


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/localization

# Localization & i18n Translation

BirJS provides an intuitive internationalization (i18n) and translation system inspired by Laravel, supporting parameter interpolation and fallback locales for use in controllers and components.

---

## 1. Translation Files

Store your translation files under `lang/` or `resources/lang/` as JSON files named after their locale code (e.g. `lang/en.json`, `lang/tr.json`):

```json
// lang/en.json
{
  "welcome": "Welcome back, {name}!",
  "auth": {
    "failed": "These credentials do not match our records.",
    "throttle": "Too many login attempts. Please try again in :seconds seconds."
  }
}
```

```json
// lang/tr.json
{
  "welcome": "Hoş geldiniz, {name}!",
  "auth": {
    "failed": "Girdiğiniz bilgiler kayıtlarımızla eşleşmiyor.",
    "throttle": "Çok fazla giriş denemesi. Lütfen :seconds saniye sonra tekrar deneyin."
  }
}
```

---

## 2. Using the `__()` Helper and `Lang` Facade

Translate keys anywhere in your application:

```typescript
import { __, Lang } from 'birframework';

// Simple translation
const hello = __('welcome', { name: 'Taylor' });
// -> "Welcome back, Taylor!"

// Dot notation nested key
const error = __('auth.failed');

// Parameter replacement supports both :param and {param}
const throttle = __('auth.throttle', { seconds: 30 });
```

### Switching Locales Dynamically

```typescript
// Change locale at runtime
Lang.setLocale('tr');
console.log(__('welcome', { name: 'Ahmet' })); // "Hoş geldiniz, Ahmet!"

// Check if a translation key exists
if (Lang.has('auth.failed')) {
  // ...
}
```

---

## 3. Translations in pages

Translate using the request locale in your controller and pass the result as page props.

```ts
Route.get('/welcome', (ctx) => ctx.inertia('Welcome', {
  message: ctx.__('welcome', { name: 'Ahmet' }),
}));
```

```tsx
export default function Welcome({ message }: { message: string }) {
  return <h1>{message}</h1>;
}
```

## 4. Context Locale Detection

In your route handlers and controllers, `ctx.locale` automatically inspects:
1. `?lang=tr` URL query parameter
2. `X-Locale` HTTP request header
3. Falls back to default `APP_LOCALE`

```typescript
Route.get('/welcome', (ctx) => {
  // Translates automatically using request's detected locale:
  const message = ctx.__('welcome', { name: 'Ferdi' });
  return ctx.json({ message, locale: ctx.locale });
});
```


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/logging

# Structured Logging & Pail

BirJS includes a unified, structured logging architecture designed for high-performance applications. It pairs file-based persistence with **Bir Pail**, an interactive CLI log tailer that streams colorized logs in real time.

---

## The Log Facade

Import the `Log` facade from `birframework` to record runtime events, security warnings, or diagnostic traces:

```ts
import { Log } from 'birframework';

// Informational events
Log.info('Order successfully processed', { orderId: 8492, amount: 149.99 });

// Warning states
Log.warning('Rate limit threshold approached', { ip: '192.168.1.1', attempts: 55 });

// Critical errors and exceptions
Log.error('Payment gateway connection failed', { gateway: 'stripe', error: err.message });

// Debug details
Log.debug('Cache query miss', { key: 'users:profile:42' });
```

---

## Log Levels

BirJS implements standard RFC 5424 log severity levels:

| Level | Method | Typical Use Case |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Emergency** | `Log.emergency(msg, ctx)` | System is unusable |
| **Alert** | `Log.alert(msg, ctx)` | Immediate action required |
| **Critical** | `Log.critical(msg, ctx)` | Critical system or database conditions |
| **Error** | `Log.error(msg, ctx)` | Runtime errors that do not require immediate action |
| **Warning** | `Log.warning(msg, ctx)` | Exceptional occurrences that are not errors |
| **Notice** | `Log.notice(msg, ctx)` | Normal but significant events |
| **Info** | `Log.info(msg, ctx)` | Interesting runtime events (user login, job dispatched) |
| **Debug** | `Log.debug(msg, ctx)` | Detailed debug information for development |

---

## Log Storage

By default, all log entries are appended asynchronously to:

```
storage/logs/bir.log
```

Log entries are formatted with ISO-8601 timestamps, log levels, and stringified JSON contextual data:

```text
[2026-11-24T16:20:00.123Z] [INFO] [HTTP] GET /api/v1/users 200 - 2.4ms {"ip":"::1"}
[2026-11-24T16:20:05.456Z] [ERROR] [Queue] Job SendInvoiceJob failed {"attempt":3,"error":"Timeout"}
```

---

## Bir Pail: Real-Time Log Streaming

Inspired by Laravel Pail, BirJS includes **Bir Pail**, a zero-dependency CLI log tailer that continuously monitors `storage/logs/bir.log` and renders incoming events with distinct ANSI badges and clean formatting:

```bash
npx bir pail
# or using the shortcut
npx bir logs
```

### Visual Category Badges

Bir Pail automatically recognizes the source and categorizes your logs with high-contrast color badges:

* <span style="color:#38bdf8;font-weight:bold;">[HTTP]</span> Cyan: Incoming HTTP requests, routes, status codes, and execution latency.
* <span style="color:#a855f7;font-weight:bold;">[Queue]</span> Purple: Job processing, retries, completions, and queue failures.
* <span style="color:#f43f5e;font-weight:bold;">[Error]</span> Rose: Uncaught exceptions, database connectivity drops, and 500 responses.
* <span style="color:#fbbf24;font-weight:bold;">[Schedule]</span> Amber: Cron task triggers and background scheduler executions.
* <span style="color:#10b981;font-weight:bold;">[Mail]</span> Emerald: Outgoing transactional emails and mailable deliveries.

---

## Dev Dashboard Integration

Bir Pail is integrated into the default development workflow. When you run:

```bash
npm run dev
```

The 4-service concurrent runner launches:
1. `server`: Your HTTP application
2. `queue`: The background queue worker
3. `logs`: **Bir Pail** live log streamer
4. `vite`: Frontend assets dev server

All four streams output to a single unified terminal window with dedicated color tags.


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/middleware

# HTTP Middleware Pipeline

Middleware provides a convenient mechanism for inspecting and filtering HTTP requests entering your application.

---

## What is Middleware?

Middleware functions wrap incoming requests in an onion-style pipeline. Common use cases include:
- Verifying authentication tokens or session cookies
- Enforcing rate limiting
- Verifying CSRF tokens on state-changing requests
- Logging request durations and response statuses

---

## Defining Custom Middleware

Create a middleware class or function implementing the `Middleware` signature:

```ts
// app/middleware/Authenticate.ts
import type { Context, Next } from 'birframework';

export async function Authenticate(ctx: Context, next: Next) {
  const token = ctx.req.headers['authorization'];

  if (!token) {
    return ctx.json({ error: 'Authentication token required' }, 401);
  }

  // Continue to the next middleware or controller
  await next();
}
```

---

## Applying Middleware

### 1. Global Middleware
Applied to every incoming request:

```ts
// app.ts
import { app } from './bootstrap.ts';
import { RequestLogger } from './app/middleware/RequestLogger.ts';

app.use(RequestLogger);
```

### 2. Route-Level Middleware
Attached to specific routes or route groups:

```ts
import { Route } from 'birframework';
import { Authenticate } from './app/middleware/Authenticate.ts';

Route.get('/dashboard', (ctx) => {
  return ctx.render('dashboard');
}).middleware(Authenticate);

Route.group({ prefix: '/admin', middleware: [Authenticate] }, () => {
  Route.get('/settings', (ctx) => ctx.render('admin/settings'));
});
```


## Response Compression (`compress`)

Compress JSON, HTML, CSS, and JS responses automatically with Brotli (`br`) or Gzip (`gzip`), while safely skipping `HEAD`, `204`/`206`/`304`, SSE (`text/event-stream`), and binary media (`audio/*`, `video/*`, `image/*`):

```ts
import { compress } from 'birframework';

app.use(compress({ threshold: 1024, brotli: true, gzip: true }));
```

## Media Streaming (`Range 206`), `ETag`, & `ctx.fileStream()`

`serveStatic()` supports `Accept-Ranges: bytes`, `206 Partial Content` / `416 Range Not Satisfiable`, and `ETag` / `304 Not Modified` out of the box for audio, video, and resumable downloads.

For authenticated or dynamic file streaming inside a controller, use `ctx.fileStream()`:

```ts
Route.get('/stream/:trackId', async (ctx) => {
  // Check auth/subscription here...
  await ctx.fileStream(`storage/tracks/${ctx.params.trackId}.mp3`);
});
```


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/migrations

# Schema & Migrations

Migrations are like version control for your database, allowing your team to define and share the application's database schema definition.

---

## Creating a Migration

Generate a new migration using the Bir CLI:

```bash
npx birframework make:migration create_posts_table
```

This creates a timestamped migration file in `database/migrations/`:

```ts
// database/migrations/2026_11_23_000001_create_posts_table.ts
import { Schema, Blueprint } from 'birframework';

export default class CreatePostsTable {
  public async up() {
    await Schema.create('posts', (table: Blueprint) => {
      table.id();
      table.string('title');
      table.string('slug').unique();
      table.text('content');
      table.integer('user_id');
      table.boolean('published').default(false);
      table.timestamps();
    });
  }

  public async down() {
    await Schema.dropIfExists('posts');
  }
}
```

---

## Running Migrations

Execute all pending migrations:

```bash
npx birframework migrate
```

Roll back the last migration batch:

```bash
npx birframework migrate:rollback
```

Reset all tables and re-run migrations from scratch:

```bash
npx birframework migrate:fresh
```

---

## Available Blueprint Column Types

| Method | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `table.id()` | Auto-incrementing Integer | Primary key |
| `table.string(name, length?)` | `VARCHAR` | Short text column |
| `table.text(name)` | `TEXT` | Multiline content column |
| `table.integer(name)` | `INTEGER` | Integer numeric column |
| `table.boolean(name)` | `BOOLEAN` | Boolean true/false column |
| `table.timestamps()` | `DATETIME` | Adds `created_at` & `updated_at` |


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/models

# Active Record ORM

BirJS provides an intuitive Active Record ORM inspired by Eloquent, allowing you to interact with database tables as expressive TypeScript classes.

---

## Defining a Model

Create model classes extending `Model`:

```ts
// app/models/User.ts
import { Model } from 'birframework';
import { Post } from './Post.ts';

export class User extends Model {
  // Table name (defaults to snake_case plural of class name: 'users')
  public static table = 'users';

  // Primary key (defaults to 'id')
  public static primaryKey = 'id';

  // Relationships
  public posts() {
    return this.hasMany(Post, 'user_id');
  }
}
```

---

## CRUD Operations

### Inserting Records

```ts
const user = await User.create({
  name: 'Ferdi Sahin',
  email: 'ferdi@birjs.com',
  role: 'admin',
});
```

### Finding & Querying

```ts
// Find by primary key
const user = await User.find(1);

// Where clauses & chaining
const admins = await User.where('role', 'admin')
  .where('is_active', true)
  .orderBy('created_at', 'DESC')
  .get();

// First matching record
const user = await User.where('email', 'ferdi@birjs.com').first();
```

### Updating Records

```ts
const user = await User.find(1);
if (user) {
  user.name = 'Updated Name';
  await user.save();
}
```

### Deleting Records

```ts
const user = await User.find(1);
if (user) {
  await user.delete();
}
```

---

## Model Lifecycle Hooks

BirJS models fire lifecycle hooks allowing you to tap into the model's lifecycle: `creating`, `created`, `saving`, `saved`, `deleting`, and `deleted`.

### Instance Method Hooks

You can define lifecycle methods directly on your Model class:

```typescript
export class Article extends Model {
  // Automatically generate slugs before record creation
  public beforeCreate() {
    if (!this.attributes['slug']) {
      this.attributes['slug'] = String(this.attributes['title'])
        .toLowerCase()
        .replace(/\s+/g, '-');
    }
  }

  public afterCreate() {
    console.log(`Article #${this.id} created successfully!`);
  }
}
```

### Static Hook Listeners

```typescript
User.saving((user) => {
  // Hash passwords or format data before saving
});

User.created(async (user) => {
  // Dispatch welcome email or notifications
});
```

---

## Soft Deletes

BirJS supports non-destructive deletions using the `softDeletes` property:

```typescript
export class Post extends Model {
  static override softDeletes = true;
}
```

### How Soft Deletes Work

When `softDeletes` is enabled:
- Calling `post.delete()` sets `deleted_at` to the current timestamp instead of removing the row from the database.
- Standard queries (`Post.all()`, `Post.find()`, `Post.where()`) automatically exclude soft-deleted records.

```typescript
const post = await Post.find(1);
await post.delete(); // Soft-deleted (deleted_at set)

console.log(post.trashed()); // true

// Will return null because record is trashed:
const normal = await Post.find(1);

// Query including soft-deleted records:
const allWithDeleted = await Post.withTrashed().where('author_id', 5).get();

// Query only soft-deleted records:
const trashedOnly = await Post.onlyTrashed().get();

// Restore a soft-deleted record:
await post.restore();

// Permanently remove from database:
await post.forceDelete();
```

---

## Pagination

Easily paginate results in your controllers:

```ts
// Returns LengthAwarePaginator with items and page metadata
const paginatedUsers = await User.paginate({ page: 1, perPage: 15 });

console.log(paginatedUsers.meta.total);        // Total count
console.log(paginatedUsers.meta.currentPage);  // 1
console.log(paginatedUsers.data);         // Current page items
```

---

## Atomic Counters (`increment` & `decrement`)

Update balances, stock counts, or retry counters atomically in SQL without race conditions:

```ts
await User.where('id', '=', userId).increment('credits', 50);
await Product.where('id', '=', productId).decrement('stock', 1);
```

---

## Idempotent Upserts (`firstOrCreate` & `updateOrCreate`)

```ts
// Find by email, or create with default balance if missing
const account = await Account.firstOrCreate(
  { email: 'customer@example.com' },
  { balance: 0, plan: 'starter' }
);

// Update existing record or create a new one
await Setting.updateOrCreate(
  { key: 'billing.currency' },
  { value: 'USD' }
);
```

---

## Chunking Large Datasets (`chunk`)

Process thousands of invoices or orders in bounded memory batches:

```ts
await Invoice.where('status', '=', 'unpaid').chunk(100, async (invoices) => {
  for (const invoice of invoices) {
    await sendReminder(invoice);
  }
});
```

---

## Many-to-Many Relationships (`belongsToMany`)

Define pivot-table relationships with `attach()`, `detach()`, `sync()`, and `get()`:

```ts
export class User extends Model {
  public roles() {
    return this.belongsToMany(Role, 'role_user', 'user_id', 'role_id');
  }
}

const user = await User.find(1);
await user?.roles().attach([1, 2]);
const roles = await user?.roles().get();
await user?.roles().sync([2, 3]);
```


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/overview

# Overview

BirJS is a TypeScript and Node.js web framework with HTTP routing, controllers, middleware, dependency injection, validation, database models, migrations, background jobs, scheduling, mail, and storage.

## Application flow

A route selects a handler. Middleware runs around that handler. Controllers read and validate the request, call application services or models, and return JSON, a redirect, or a rendered page.

## Rendering profiles

The Inertia profile uses Preact pages with server rendering and browser hydration. Its client Link and router helpers request page data without a full document navigation. The server-rendered profile returns TSX/JSX HTML through ctx.render.

## Database and services

SQLite uses Node's built-in node:sqlite. PostgreSQL and MySQL use optional pg and mysql2 packages. Queue workers and schedulers run as separate processes. Cache and session storage choices determine whether state is process-local or shared.

## Deployment

Run the application as a persistent Node.js process or export its serverless handler. Persistent processes retain in-memory state while running. Serverless instances can restart independently, so shared state requires suitable external storage.

Start with [Installation](/docs/installation), then read [Directory structure](/docs/directory-structure) and [Routing](/docs/routing).


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/providers

# Service Providers & Plugins

Service Providers are the central place for configuring and bootstrapping applications in BirJS. If you are familiar with Laravel's `ServiceProvider`, BirJS brings the exact same clean, modular architecture to modern TypeScript and Node.js.

---

## What is a Service Provider?

Service Providers allow you to encapsulate related logic (registering container bindings, setting up third-party SDKs, defining view globals, configuring event listeners, or hooking into request lifecycles) into reusable, self-contained classes.

Each Service Provider follows a two-phase lifecycle:

1. **`register()`**: Use this method to bind things into the Service Container (`app.container.singleton()` or `app.container.bind()`). In this method, you should **never** attempt to use services provided by other providers, because they may not have been registered yet.
2. **`boot()`**: Called after **all** providers have executed their `register()` methods. Here you can safely access any service, register view shared data, or initialize listeners.

---

## Creating a Service Provider

You can quickly scaffold a new Service Provider using the Bir CLI:

```bash
bir make:provider PaymentServiceProvider
```

This generates `app/providers/PaymentServiceProvider.ts`:

```typescript
import { ServiceProvider } from 'birframework';
import type { Application } from 'birframework';
import { StripeGateway } from '../services/StripeGateway.js';

export class PaymentServiceProvider extends ServiceProvider {
  /**
   * Register container bindings.
   */
  public register(): void {
    this.app.container.singleton('payment.gateway', () => {
      const apiKey = process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY || '';
      return new StripeGateway(apiKey);
    });
  }

  /**
   * Bootstrap services after all providers are registered.
   */
  public boot(): void {
    // You can share data with views, attach events, etc.
    console.log('[PaymentServiceProvider] Booted successfully.');
  }
}
```

---

## Registering Providers in Your Application

You can register Service Providers directly on your `Application` instance:

```typescript
// app.ts or bootstrap/app.ts
import { Application } from 'birframework';
import { PaymentServiceProvider } from './app/providers/PaymentServiceProvider.js';

const app = new Application();

// Register the provider
app.register(PaymentServiceProvider);

export default app;
```

### Accessing Registered Services from Container

Anywhere in your controllers or middleware:

```typescript
// app/controllers/CheckoutController.ts
import type { Context } from 'birframework';
import { StripeGateway } from '../services/StripeGateway.js';

export class CheckoutController {
  async process(ctx: Context) {
    const gateway = app.container.make<StripeGateway>('payment.gateway');
    const result = await gateway.charge((await ctx.body()).amount);
    return ctx.json({ success: true, result });
  }
}
```

---

## Functional Plugins (Micro-Modules)

If you have lightweight logic or want to publish a third-party npm package for BirJS, you can use **functional plugins**:

```typescript
import type { Application } from 'birframework';

export function myAnalyticsPlugin(app: Application, options: { trackingId: string }) {
  // Hook into router or add global middleware
  app.use(async (ctx, next) => {
    ctx.header('X-Tracking-ID', options.trackingId);
    await next();
  });
}
```

Registering a functional plugin:

```typescript
app.register(myAnalyticsPlugin, { trackingId: 'GA-999999' });
```

---

## Provider lifecycle

Use `register()` for container bindings and `boot()` for initialization after providers have registered. The provider receives `this.app`, with access to its container, router, and middleware registration.

The controller example above assumes you export your Application instance from a bootstrap module and import it as `app`. Keep the listening entry separate when importing the application into tests.


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/queues

# Background Queues

Offload time-consuming tasks — such as sending emails, image resizing, or AI processing — to background queue workers.

---

## Defining a Job

Generate a new job class using the CLI:

```bash
npx birframework make:job SendWelcomeEmailJob
```

Implement the `handle()` method:

```ts
// app/jobs/SendWelcomeEmailJob.ts
import { Job } from 'birframework';
import { Mail } from 'birframework';

export class SendWelcomeEmailJob extends Job {
  constructor(public user: { name: string; email: string }) {
    super();
  }

  public async handle() {
    await Mail.to(this.user.email).raw('<p>Welcome to BirJS.</p>', {
      subject: 'Welcome to BirJS',
    });
  }
}
```

---

## Dispatching Jobs

Dispatch jobs from your controllers or services:

```ts
import { dispatch } from 'birframework';
import { SendWelcomeEmailJob } from '../jobs/SendWelcomeEmailJob.ts';

// Dispatch immediately to default queue
await dispatch(new SendWelcomeEmailJob(user));

// Dispatch with delay
await dispatch(new SendWelcomeEmailJob(user).delay(60));
```

---

## Running the Queue Worker

Start processing queued jobs in the background:

```bash
npx birframework queue:work
```

The worker continuously polls the queue table, executes job `handle()` methods, and manages retry attempts with retries on failures.

---

## Failed Jobs & Retry Management

When a job exceeds its maximum retry attempts (`tries`), it is automatically recorded in the `_failed_jobs` table instead of being discarded:

```bash
# List all failed jobs with timestamps and IDs
npx bir queue:failed

# Retry a specific failed job or all failed jobs
npx bir queue:retry 42
npx bir queue:retry all

# Clear the failed jobs table
npx bir queue:flush
```

## Register jobs in the worker process

Create `app/jobs/index.ts` (or `.js`) and register each job class. The CLI worker imports this file before processing persisted jobs.

```ts
import { Queue } from 'birframework';
import { SendWelcomeEmailJob } from './SendWelcomeEmailJob.js';

Queue.register(SendWelcomeEmailJob);
```

Job properties are persisted as JSON. Use serializable values and resolve database records inside `handle()` when fresh data is needed. Delay values are seconds.


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/resources

# API Resources & JSON Transformation

When building modern APIs, you often need an abstraction layer that sits between your database models and the JSON responses actually returned to users or frontend applications.

BirJS's **JsonResource** provides a clean, expressive transformation layer inspired by Eloquent API Resources, enabling precise control over field exposure, relationships, pagination, and conditional attributes.

---

## 1. Creating a Resource

To create a resource, extend `JsonResource` and implement the `toArray()` method:

```typescript
import { JsonResource, type Context } from 'birframework';
import type { User } from '../models/User.js';

export class UserResource extends JsonResource<User> {
  public toArray(ctx?: Context) {
    return {
      id: this.resource.id,
      name: this.resource.name,
      email: this.resource.email,
      created_at: this.resource.created_at,
    };
  }
}
```

---

## 2. Using Resources in Routes and Controllers

You can transform a single model or a collection of models:

### Single Model Transformation

```typescript
import { Route } from 'birframework';
import { User } from '../models/User.js';
import { UserResource } from '../resources/UserResource.js';

Route.get('/api/users/:id', async (ctx) => {
  const user = await User.find(ctx.params.id);
  if (!user) return ctx.json({ error: 'User not found' }, 404);

  return UserResource.make(user);
});
```

By default, single resources are wrapped inside a top-level `data` key:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": 1,
    "name": "Jane Doe",
    "email": "jane@example.com",
    "created_at": "2026-11-23T10:00:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

### Resource Collections

To transform an array or collection of models, use the static `collection()` method:

```typescript
Route.get('/api/users', async (ctx) => {
  const users = await User.all();
  return UserResource.collection(users);
});
```

```json
{
  "data": [
    { "id": 1, "name": "Jane Doe", "email": "jane@example.com" },
    { "id": 2, "name": "John Smith", "email": "john@example.com" }
  ]
}
```

---

## 3. Preserving Paginator Metadata

When passing a `LengthAwarePaginator` (returned by `Model.paginate()`) to `collection()`, BirJS automatically transforms the items while preserving total counts, current page, and pagination links:

```typescript
Route.get('/api/users', async (ctx) => {
  const page = Number(ctx.query.page) || 1;
  const paginatedUsers = await User.paginate({ page, perPage: 15 });

  return UserResource.collection(paginatedUsers);
});
```

Response:

```json
{
  "data": [
    { "id": 1, "name": "Jane Doe", "email": "jane@example.com" }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "total": 50,
    "perPage": 15,
    "currentPage": 1,
    "lastPage": 4,
    "from": 1,
    "to": 15
  },
  "links": {
    "first": "?page=1",
    "last": "?page=4",
    "prev": null,
    "next": "?page=2"
  }
}
```

---

## 4. Conditional Attributes

BirJS provides `when()` and `whenNotNull()` helpers inside `JsonResource` to include attributes only when specific conditions are met (e.g. admin privileges or non-empty relationships):

```typescript
export class UserResource extends JsonResource<User> {
  public toArray(ctx?: Context) {
    const isAdmin = ctx?.session?.get('is_admin') === true;

    return {
      id: this.resource.id,
      name: this.resource.name,
      email: this.resource.email,

      // Only included if isAdmin is true
```
