```typescript
      secret_token: this.when(isAdmin, this.resource.secret_token),

      // Only included if phone is not null/undefined
      phone: this.whenNotNull(this.resource.phone),
    };
  }
}
```

---

## 5. Adding Top-Level Metadata

Attach additional root-level metadata (such as status codes, copyright, or runtime metrics) using the `.additional()` chain:

```typescript
return UserResource.make(user).additional({
  status: 'success',
  meta: {
    cached: false,
    version: '1.0',
  },
});
```

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": 1,
    "name": "Jane Doe"
  },
  "status": "success",
  "meta": {
    "cached": false,
    "version": "1.0"
  }
}
```

---

## 6. Disabling Data Wrapping

If you prefer flat JSON output without the top-level `data` key, call `withoutWrapping()` on the resource class:

```typescript
UserResource.withoutWrapping();
return UserResource.make(user);
```

Output:

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "name": "Jane Doe",
  "email": "jane@example.com"
}
```


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/routing

# Routing & Parameters

BirJS features an intuitive, expressive router inspired by Laravel, engineered for sub-millisecond route dispatching.

---

## Basic Route Definition

Define routes in `routes/web.ts` (for HTML views) or `routes/api.ts` (for REST endpoints):

```ts
import { Route, auth } from 'birframework';

// Basic GET route returning JSON
Route.get('/ping', (ctx) => {
  return ctx.json({ status: 'pong', time: Date.now() });
});

// Basic POST route
Route.post('/contact', async (ctx) => {
  const body = await ctx.body();
  return ctx.json({ success: true, message: 'Message received' });
});
```

---

## Route Parameters

Capture dynamic parameters in URLs using the `:param` syntax:

```ts
// Mandatory route parameter
Route.get('/users/:id', async (ctx) => {
  const userId = ctx.params.id;
  return ctx.json({ id: userId });
});

// Multiple parameters
Route.get('/posts/:slug/comments/:commentId', (ctx) => {
  const { slug, commentId } = ctx.params;
  return ctx.json({ slug, commentId });
});
```

---

## Named Routes

Name routes for identification in route listings and application tooling:

```ts
Route.get('/users/profile', (ctx) => {
  return ctx.render('profile');
}).name('user.profile');

// Use the registered URL when linking to this route.
```

---

## Route Groups & Prefixes

Organize related endpoints with route prefixes and shared middleware:

```ts
Route.group({ prefix: '/api/v1', middleware: [auth()] }, () => {
  Route.get('/me', (ctx) => ctx.json(ctx.user));
  Route.get('/orders', (ctx) => ctx.json([]));
});
```

---

## HTTP Verbs Supported

| Method | Helper Method | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `Route.get(path, handler)` | Fetch data or render page |
| `POST` | `Route.post(path, handler)` | Create new resource |
| `PUT` | `Route.put(path, handler)` | Replace existing resource |
| `PATCH` | `Route.patch(path, handler)` | Partially update resource |
| `DELETE` | `Route.delete(path, handler)` | Remove resource |


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/scheduler

# Task Scheduler

Register tasks and start the scheduler in the same process. The CLI schedule:work and schedule:run commands do not automatically import your application's schedule definitions.

## Application entry point

```ts
// app/console/scheduler.ts
import { Schedule } from 'birframework';

Schedule.call(async () => {
  console.log('Scheduled check');
}, 'Scheduled check').everyMinute();

await Schedule.work();
```

```bash
node --import tsx app/console/scheduler.ts
```

Use `Schedule.work({ once: true })` to run due tasks once. In a JavaScript project omit the tsx loader and use a .js file.

## Frequencies

Supported helpers are everySecond(), everyMinute(), everyFiveMinutes(), everyTenMinutes(), everyThirtyMinutes(), hourly(), daily(), and dailyAt('14:30'). Interval helpers measure elapsed time since the previous execution. dailyAt checks the local process time.

## Queue jobs

```ts
import { Schedule } from 'birframework';
import { BackupJob } from '../jobs/BackupJob.js';

Schedule.job(new BackupJob()).dailyAt('02:00');
```

Schedule.job dispatches to the queue. Register the class in app/jobs/index.ts and run a queue worker to execute it.

## Prevent overlap

```ts
Schedule.call(async () => {
  await synchronizeCatalog();
}, 'Synchronize catalog').everyFiveMinutes().withoutOverlapping(3600);
```

withoutOverlapping uses exclusive files under storage/framework/locks. Processes coordinate only when sharing the lock directory. A task exceeding the lock TTL can overlap a later execution. Keep descriptions stable and distinct for tasks that need independent locks.


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/security

# Security

BirJS provides session signing, CSRF middleware, password hashing, rate limiting, encryption, and authorization helpers. Register the middleware required by your application explicitly.

## Application key

```bash
npx bir key:generate
```

Keep APP_KEY private and stable across workers and deployments. Session signing can use a temporary process secret when the key is missing, which invalidates sessions after restarts. Crypt and SignedUrl require a configured key.

## Sessions and CSRF

```ts
import { sessionMiddleware, csrf, csrfToken, Route } from 'birframework';

app.use(sessionMiddleware());
app.use(csrf());

Route.get('/profile', (ctx) => ctx.inertia('Profile', {
  csrfToken: csrfToken(ctx),
}));
```

Register sessions before CSRF. The csrf middleware checks state-changing requests on routes where it runs. Read-only GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS requests are exempt.

```tsx
export function ProfileForm({ csrfToken }: { csrfToken: string }) {
  return <form method="POST" action="/profile">
    <input type="hidden" name="_token" value={csrfToken} />
    <input name="name" />
    <button type="submit">Save</button>
  </form>;
}
```

Fetch requests can send `X-CSRF-TOKEN` or `X-XSRF-TOKEN`. The body field is `_token`. Obtain it from server-provided props or an explicitly rendered meta tag.

## Rate limiting

```ts
import { Route, rateLimit } from 'birframework';

Route.post('/login', loginHandler).middleware(rateLimit({ max: 5, windowMs: 60000 }));
```

The built-in limiter is process-local. Proxy headers are trusted only when configured. Use an appropriate shared limit at your infrastructure layer when running multiple instances.

## Mass assignment and SQL

```ts
import { Model } from 'birframework';

export class User extends Model {
  static table = 'users';
  static fillable = ['name', 'email'];
}
```

Use validated fields and an explicit fillable allowlist. Query builder values use bindings. Raw SQL passed to DB.raw or DB.execute remains the application's responsibility. Pass values separately as parameters.

## Security headers

Application registers securityHeaders by default. The default response headers include X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and X-XSS-Protection 0.

## Encryption and signed URLs

```ts
import { Crypt, SignedUrl, signed, Route } from 'birframework';

const encrypted = Crypt.encrypt({ apiKey: 'example' });
const credentials = Crypt.decrypt<{ apiKey: string }>(encrypted);
const url = SignedUrl.sign('/invoices/1042/pdf', 1800);
Route.get('/invoices/:id/pdf', downloadHandler).middleware(signed());
```

## Authorization

```ts
import { Gate } from 'birframework';

Gate.define('cancel-invoice', (user, invoice) => user?.id === invoice.userId);
await Gate.authorize('cancel-invoice', user, invoice);
```

## Webhook signatures

Read the original request bytes with `await ctx.rawBody()`. Verify the received signature using the provider's exact signing format and a timing-safe comparison before processing the event. Calculating an HMAC alone does not authenticate a webhook.


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/storage

# File Storage

BirJS provides an expressive file storage abstraction layer for local disks and cloud drivers.

---

## Basic File Operations

Use the `Storage` facade to store, retrieve, and delete files:

```ts
import { Storage } from 'birframework';

// Write content to a file
await Storage.put('avatars/user-1.jpg', fileBuffer);

// Check if a file exists
if (await Storage.exists('avatars/user-1.jpg')) {
  // Read file contents
  const content = await Storage.get('avatars/user-1.jpg');
}

// Delete a file
await Storage.delete('avatars/user-1.jpg');
```

---

## Multipart File Uploads

BirJS natively parses `multipart/form-data` uploads with zero external dependencies. In your controllers, access uploaded files via `ctx.file('field_name')`:

```tsx
export function AvatarForm({ csrfToken }: { csrfToken: string }) {
  return <form action="/profile/avatar" method="POST" encType="multipart/form-data">
    <input type="hidden" name="_token" value={csrfToken} />
    <input type="file" name="avatar" accept="image/*" required />
    <button type="submit">Upload Avatar</button>
  </form>;
}
```

Pass the current CSRF token from the controller to the page.


```typescript
// app/controllers/ProfileController.ts
import { Route } from 'birframework';

export class ProfileController {
  public async uploadAvatar(ctx) {
    const file = await ctx.file('avatar');

    if (!file || !file.isValid()) {
      return ctx.json({ error: 'Please choose a valid file' }, 422);
    }

    // Inspect file metadata
    console.log(file.originalName); // "photo.png"
    console.log(file.mimeType);     // "image/png"
    console.log(file.extension());    // "png"
    console.log(file.size);         // Size in bytes

    // 1. Store with auto-generated unique filename:
    const storedPath = await file.store('avatars');
    // -> "avatars/a7f8b9...png" in storage/app/avatars/

    // 2. Or store on the public web disk with a custom name:
    const customPath = await file.storeAs('avatars', `user-${ctx.user?.id}.png`, 'public');

    return ctx.json({ success: true, path: storedPath });
  }
}
```

---

## Storage Directory Structure

By default, files are stored under the `storage/app/` directory:

```
storage/
├── app/
│   ├── public/          # Publicly accessible static assets
│   └── private/         # Private files & documents
├── logs/                # Application error logs
└── database.sqlite      # Default SQLite database
```

---

## Mailing & Email System

BirJS provides a clean email delivery API modeled directly on Laravel Mailables:

### 1. Generating a Mailable Class

Use the CLI generator:

```bash
bir make:mail WelcomeMail
```

This generates `app/mail/WelcomeMail.ts`:

```typescript
import { Mailable } from 'birframework';

export class WelcomeMail extends Mailable {
  constructor(public user: { name: string; email: string }) {
    super();
    this.subject('Welcome to BirJS!')
        .from('hello@birjs.com', 'BirJS Team');
  }

  public async content(): Promise<string> {
    // Renders views/emails/welcome.tsx with data
    return this.view('emails/welcome', { user: this.user });
  }
}
```

### 2. Sending Emails

Send emails from anywhere in your application:

```typescript
import { Mail } from 'birframework';
import { WelcomeMail } from './mail/WelcomeMail.js';

// Send a class-based Mailable:
await Mail.to('jane@example.com').send(new WelcomeMail(user));

// Or send a quick raw HTML email:
await Mail.to('jane@example.com').raw('<h1>Your verification code is 123456</h1>', {
  subject: 'Verify your account'
});
```

### 3. Testing with `Mail.fake()`

Verify emails are sent in automated tests without actually delivering to SMTP:

```typescript
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { Mail } from 'birframework';

test('registration sends welcome email', async () => {
  Mail.fake();

  await registerUserAction({ email: 'test@example.com' });

  const sent = Mail.sent();
  assert.strictEqual(sent.length, 1);
  assert.strictEqual(sent[0].to, 'test@example.com');

  Mail.restore();
});
```

### 4. Production Mail Drivers (`Resend` & `SMTP`) & Attachments

BirJS ships with zero-dependency **Resend API** and **raw SMTP (TCP/TLS)** drivers, plus `.attach()` support for PDF invoices:

```typescript
import { Mail, Mailable } from 'birframework';

// Configure automatically from .env (MAIL_MAILER=resend|smtp|log)
Mail.configureFromEnv();

// Or configure explicitly:
Mail.useResend(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY!);
// Mail.useSmtp({ host: 'smtp.example.com', port: 465, user: '...', pass: '...', secure: true });

class InvoiceMail extends Mailable {
  content() {
    return '<p>Your invoice PDF is attached.</p>';
  }
}

await Mail.to('customer@example.com').send(
  new InvoiceMail()
    .subject('Invoice #1042')
    .attach({ filename: 'invoice-1042.pdf', content: pdfBuffer, contentType: 'application/pdf' })
);
```



Source: https://birjs.com/docs/testing

# HTTP Testing & Test Runner

BirJS includes a built-in HTTP testing assistant inspired by Laravel and Pest. You can write expressive, fluid integration and feature tests with zero third-party testing bloat.

---

## 1. Running Tests (`bir test`)

Run your entire test suite from the terminal with a single command:

```bash
npx birframework test
```

You can also filter tests by file name:

```bash
npx birframework test auth
npx birframework test upload
```

---

## 2. The `createTestClient` Assistant

Use `createTestClient(app)` to send requests through your application without managing manual network ports:

```typescript
import { test, describe, before, after } from 'node:test';
import { Application, createTestClient, type TestClient } from 'birframework';
import { app } from '../bootstrap.js';

describe('Authentication Feature Tests', () => {
  let client: TestClient;

  before(() => { client = createTestClient(app); });

  after(async () => {
    await client?.close();
  });

  test('guests can view login page', async () => {
    const res = await client.get('/login');

    res.assertOk()
       .assertSee('Sign In')
       .assertDontSee('Dashboard');
  });

  test('valid login redirects to dashboard', async () => {
    const res = await client.post('/login', {
      email: 'user@birjs.com',
      password: 'password123',
    });

    res.assertRedirect('/dashboard');
  });
});
```

---

## 3. Available Response Assertions

The `TestResponse` returned by `client.get()`, `client.post()`, etc. provides a rich set of chainable assertions:

### Status Assertions

```typescript
res.assertOk();              // Status 200
res.assertCreated();         // Status 201
res.assertNotFound();        // Status 404
res.assertForbidden();       // Status 403
res.assertUnauthorized();    // Status 401
res.assertUnprocessable();   // Status 422
res.assertStatus(code);      // Custom status check
```

### Redirect Assertions

```typescript
// Assert response was a redirect (301, 302, 307, 308)
res.assertRedirect();

// Assert response redirected to an exact path
res.assertRedirect('/dashboard');
```

### Content & JSON Assertions

```typescript
// Assert response text includes / excludes substring
res.assertSee('Welcome');
res.assertDontSee('Error occurred');

// Assert JSON body matches expected subset
res.assertJson({ success: true, count: 5 });

// Retrieve parsed bodies directly
const data = res.json();
const html = res.text();
```

---

## 4. Simulating Authenticated Requests (`actingAs`)

Simulate logged-in user requests without repeating login forms:

```typescript
test('authenticated user can view protected dashboard', async () => {
  client = createTestClient(app);

  const res = await client.actingAs(user).get('/dashboard');
  res.assertOk().assertSee('Welcome, ' + user.name);
});
```

The bootstrap module in these examples exports an Application with routes and middleware registered, without calling listen(). Configure a test database and seed the user before testing login. Include a CSRF token when the tested route uses CSRF middleware.


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/validation

# Request Validation

BirJS includes a zero-dependency schema validation engine featuring Laravel-style pipe validation rules.

---

## Basic Validation

Call `ctx.validate(rules)` inside any controller action or route closure:

```ts
import { Route } from 'birframework';

Route.post('/register', async (ctx) => {
  const data = await ctx.validate({
    name: 'required|min:3|max:50',
    email: 'required|email',
    password: 'required|min:8',
    age: 'numeric|min:18',
  });

  // `data` contains fields selected by the validation rules.
  return ctx.json({ status: 'ok', user: data });
});
```

---

## Form Request Classes

For complex validation scenarios or to keep controllers thin and focused, use **Form Requests**:

```bash
npx birframework make:request StoreUserRequest
```

This generates `app/requests/StoreUserRequest.ts`:

```typescript
import { FormRequest, type ValidationRules } from 'birframework';

export class StoreUserRequest extends FormRequest<{ name: string; email: string }> {
  /**
   * Determine if the user is authorized to perform this action.
   */
  public override async authorize(): Promise<boolean> {
    return this.ctx.session?.has('user_id') === true;
  }

  /**
   * Mutate or prepare inputs prior to validation.
   */
  public override async prepareForValidation(): Promise<void> {
    const body = (await this.ctx.body()) || {};
    if (body.email) {
      body.email = body.email.trim().toLowerCase();
    }
  }

  /**
   * Get the validation rules.
   */
  public override rules(): ValidationRules {
    return {
      name: 'required|min:3',
      email: 'required|email',
    };
  }
}
```

### Using Form Requests in Controllers

Use `ctx.validateWith(RequestClass)`:

```typescript
export class UserController {
  public async store(ctx: Context) {
    // 1. Checks authorize() -> throws 403 Forbidden if false
    // 2. Runs prepareForValidation()
    // 3. Runs rules() -> throws 422 Unprocessable if invalid
    // 4. Returns strictly typed validated data:
    const validated = await ctx.validateWith(StoreUserRequest);

    const user = await User.create(validated);
    return ctx.json({ user }, 201);
  }
}
```

---

## Error Handling

When validation fails, BirJS automatically stops request execution:
- **API / JSON Requests**: Returns a `422 Unprocessable Content` response with structured error messages.
- **Web Form Requests**: With an active session and an HTML Accept header, flashes errors and redirects to a same-origin form URL. Without a session, returns JSON errors.

Example JSON error response:

```json
{
  "message": "The given data was invalid.",
  "errors": {
    "email": ["The email must be a valid email address."],
    "password": ["The password must be at least 8 characters."]
  }
}
```

---

## Available Validation Rules

| Rule | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `required` | Field must be present and not empty | `'title': 'required'` |
| `email` | Must be a valid email address | `'email': 'required\|email'` |
| `min:n` | Minimum string length or numeric value | `'password': 'min:8'` |
| `max:n` | Maximum string length or numeric value | `'username': 'max:20'` |
| `numeric` | Value must be a valid number | `'price': 'numeric'` |
| `boolean` | Must be true, false, 0, or 1 | `'terms': 'required\|boolean'` |
| `in:a,b,c` | Value must be in the specified list | `'status': 'in:draft,published'` |


Source: https://birjs.com/docs/views

# Views and Page Rendering

BirJS renders Preact components written in TSX or JSX. Choose the Inertia profile for client navigation and interactive pages, or the server-rendered profile for request-by-request HTML rendering.

## Inertia pages

Place page components in `views/pages/`. Controllers provide serializable props with `ctx.inertia()`.

```ts
Route.get('/', (ctx) => ctx.inertia('Welcome', { title: 'Welcome' }));
```

```tsx
// views/pages/Welcome.tsx
export default function Welcome({ title }: { title: string }) {
  return <main><h1>{title}</h1></main>;
}
```

Use the generated `Link` component from `resources/js/bir-inertia` for client navigation. A normal HTML anchor performs browser navigation.

## Server-rendered views

Place named views directly under `views/` in the server-rendered profile. Return them with `ctx.render()`.

```ts
Route.get('/', (ctx) => ctx.render('Welcome', { title: 'Welcome' }));
```

A server-rendered view uses the same TSX/JSX component syntax. Use the generated layout to include the document structure and assets.

## Generating a view

```bash
npx bir make:view Welcome
```

The generator detects the project language and whether `views/pages/` exists. It creates a `.tsx` or `.jsx` component in the appropriate directory.

## Layouts and reusable components

Keep shared page structure in `views/layouts/` and interface elements in `views/components/`. Pass content as props and children. See [Components](/docs/components) and [Inertia](/docs/inertia) for examples.

## Rendering data

Use JSX expressions, JavaScript conditionals, and array mapping. JSX text expressions escape user text. Render Markdown through an explicitly configured parser and sanitize untrusted HTML before inserting it into a page.
